en.headline: Security guard given suspended sentence for blank-vote comments
en.dek: A 38-year-old man was sentenced to two months’ jail suspended for three years after pleading guilty to publicly inciting others to cast invalid votes during the 2025 Legislative Council election.
body: A security guard was sentenced at West Kowloon Magistrates’ Courts on Monday to two months in prison, suspended for three years, for posting online comments that supported casting blank votes during last year’s Legislative Council election.

Lam Ramirez Kuk-wai, 38, pleaded guilty to one count of engaging in illegal conduct by publicly inciting others to cast an invalid vote by activity in public during an election period. The court heard he posted three comments under the account name “Steve Lam” beneath a media outlet’s social media post dated 28 October 2025 that reported a warning by the Secretary for Security.

The comments included “Cast blank votes, don’t register as voters” and “It’s actually fine not to vote. It makes no difference whether you vote or not now.” Principal Magistrate Don So Man-lung noted that similar offences generally attract immediate custody to protect electoral integrity, but took into account that Lam was a first-time offender and the offending period was relatively short.

zh.headline: 保安員網上鼓吹投白票判囚兩月緩刑三年
zh.dek: 38歲男子承認在2025年立法會選舉期間公開煽惑他人投無效票，西九龍裁判法院周一判處監禁兩個月，緩刑三年。
body: 一名保安員周一在西九龍裁判法院因網上留言支持投白票，被判監禁兩個月，緩刑三年。
38歲林姓被告承認一項在選舉期間以公開活動煽惑他人投無效票的控罪。案情指他在2025年10月28日一則報道保安局局長警告的社交媒體帖文下，以「Steve Lam」帳戶發表三則留言，包括「投白票，不要登記做選民」及「其實不投票都沒所謂，現在投不投票都一樣」。
主任裁判官蘇文隆指同類罪行一般須即時監禁以維護選舉制度完整，但考慮被告屬初犯及犯罪期間相對短暫，最終判處監禁兩個月、緩刑三年。
